The Screening Room

Six moves for the new Garran Hill. Real photographs, real scroll. Feel each one. Keep what deserves the house.

Scroll
Move One

The diptych reveal. Two frames, offset, arriving like a turned page.

Move Two

The dissolve. 1916 becomes now, at the pace of your own hand.

In 1916, those were saplings. Now they are a forest.
Move Three

The film strip. A room told in frames. The page pauses, the kitchen unfolds.

Drag · Swipe · Arrow

Move Four

The viewing room. Tap a photograph. The page falls away.

Move Five

The held frame. One photograph stays. The years pass across it.

He bought the land in February 1913. Six weeks later, Wilson sent him to London.Walter Hines Page · 1855–1918

The house rose in 1916 while he served at the Court of St James's. He wrote home about the farm, letter after letter.

He named it Garran Hill. He never spent a night here.

Move Six

The breath. Between chapters, the page goes quiet.

The house was here before you arrived. It will be here after.

The Verdict

Which of these belongs to Garran Hill?

Tell Coco which moves stay, which go, and which need to be turned up or down. The kit is built from your answers.
